utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-69-T. The Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber apologises first of all for the late start. I was dealing with a matter which I'd like to briefly discuss with the parties. Next week we are scheduled to sit on Wednesday and Thursday. The Chamber is exploring the possibilities of sitting on Tuesday and Wednesday instead of Wednesday and Thursday for reasons which are foreign to this case. It is still to be decided if we would sit on Tuesday, whether that would be morning or afternoon. The Chamber always tries to schedule the Stanisic/Simatovic case in the afternoons, which was, of course, at the time primarily inspired by creating an opportunity for medical reports to be produced during the morning hours. That may not be such an urgent reason any more under the present circumstances, and we might further consider that. But as matters stand now I would just like to know whether it would cause any problem with the Defence teams to sit on Tuesday rather than on Thursday. And I have to admit we have already sought information from the Prosecution, because the Prosecution of course had an additional problem, that is to secure the presence of the witness, which is even more important. SO we checked that with the Prosecution. Prosecution has no problems, as I understand, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I wouldn't characterise it as no problems, Your Honours, but they are surmountable problems, and we can have a witness here on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I wonder whether there's any problem as far as the Stanisic or the the Simatovic Defence is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No problem for us, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No problem, neither morning or afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem for us either, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your co-operative attitude. We'll then further proceed to see whether this can be scheduled. I would like to before we call -- before the next witness will be called, I would like to turn into closed session, or private session, but that's the same in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could I seek contact with the representative of the Registry at the other side of the videolink. Can you see us, can you hear us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. We are here in the field office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in the field office, you can see us and you can hear us apparently.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can also see and hear you you. Could you tell us who is present in the room of the videolink.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] We have two representatives of the Registry and one technician, Your Honours. And the witness is present as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And I see that the witness is present already. Then, witness, can you hear me and can you see me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by the Registrar. May I invite you to stand and to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Witness, you'll be first examined by Mr. Weber. Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Examination by Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Marinovic. My name is Adam Weber. I just wanted to confirm with you if you can see me by the way of videolink.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please introduce yourself to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Ante Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the microphone be put closer to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic, did you provide a statement to an investigator from the ICTY on the date of 30 September 2000?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you review a statement that you provided to an investigator from the ICTY on the 30th of September, 2000, prior to testifying here today?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you provide testimony in the case of Prosecutor versus Milan Martic on the date of 23 March 2006?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had the opportunity prior to testifying here today to review your prior statement and your testimony from the Martic case in your own language?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: I have today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you were asked the same questions that you were asked during your previous statement and testimony, would you provide the same answers in substance?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it depends. I may have omitted something, forgotten something, but for 80 per cent, I think I would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, are the answers that you provided in your previous statement in previous testimony accurate?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders 65 ter 5325, the 2000 ICTY statement, and 65 ter 5324, the previous testimony from the Martic case into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar, could you assign numbers, first to the ICTY statement, second to the Martic transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. 65 ter 5235 is now Exhibit P490. 65 ter 5234 is now Exhibit P491.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P490 and P491 are admitted into evidence. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders the one associated exhibit to Exhibit P491. It is a map which has been listed under 65 ter 5326 with the ERN of 0501-3942.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar, the map would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 5326 will be now Exhibit P492.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P492 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Pursuant to the Trial Chamber's instructions of the 18th of February, 2010, the Prosecution at this time requests leave to present a public summary of the evidence of Ante Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, has the witness been informed about the purpose of -- then I'll do that first. Witness, Mr. Weber will read a summary of your testimony, summary of your evidence, that is, what is found in your statement and what is found in the transcript in the Martic case. This is not the evidence, but if a summary would not be read, the public would not know what your testimony was about, so that's the one and only purpose of reading this summary. Just wait until it's over and then Mr. Weber may have some additional questions for you. Please proceed Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ante Marinovic is a Croat male, age 31, at the time of the events in 1991. The witness was a reserve police officer in Benkovac and lived in the village of Bruska, the village of Bruska was almost exclusively a Croat village. Mr. Marinovic observed in the months leading up to the war, that the Serbs from the surrounding villages received weapons from the JNA. The first barricades were erected in February of 1991, and the Croat inhabitants of the village were harassed at these roadblocks. In the summer of 1991, military vehicles continually passed through the village, this occurred during the attack on Krusevo. Every two or three days, the witness observed Serb paramilitaries come to Bruska. These paramilitaries went to the village square or other places and threatened the Croat inhabitants. These paramilitaries told the Croat villagers that this was Serb country and that they should leave. The village of Bruska was attacked on the 21 of December, 1991. At around 8.00 in the evening, three men of Martic's police with Krajina milicija insignias on their uniform broke into the home of the witness. The witness; his father, Roko Marinovic; his brother, Dusko Marinovic; and his uncle, Petar Marinovic; along with a Serb friend by the name of Sveto Draca, who had refused to join the milicija, were ordered out of the house and lined up against the wall. When -- I don't know if the witness said something right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think he said something, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's wait until Mr. Weber has finished reading his summary. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When Petar and Sveto tried to run away, they were shot and killed by the Martic's police. The witness's father and brother were shot in the head. The witness was shot seven times and survived. He succeeded to flee to relatives he had in Bijeljina. They took him to the Benkovac hospital where his wounds were treated before being taken to the Knin hospital to undergo surgery. The witness underwent recovery at the Knin hospital where member of Martic's police came and questioned him. At one point, the witness heard the police officer state "this Ustasha must be slaughtered." The witness provides evidence that besides the four persons he saw killed, Ika Marinovic, Stana Marinovic, Josip Marinovic, Manda Marinovic, Krste Marinovic, and Draginja Marinovic, all relatives of the witness were also killed on the date of 21 December, 1991. The witness provides evidence that after all of the Croat villagers had left Bruska, Captain Dragan came to the village and established a training centre called training centre Alfa in Bruska. That completes the summary of the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weber. Any additional questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I do have some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic, the Prosecution would like to ask you some questions regarding events that occurred prior to the date of the 21st of December, 1991. On page 2474 of Exhibit P491, you were asked whether you had seen any posters or anything from the SDS that led you to believe that the SDS had support in your area. You answered that there were posters all over the place. My question, sir, is could you please tell us approximately when did you first see these posters in the area of Bruska?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when the campaign, the election campaign began.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately when did this election campaign begin?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, a month before the election in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what month that was?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: It was May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did these posters say on them?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: There was just a picture of Jovan Raskovic and SDS on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 2475 of Exhibit P491 you state that Sveto Draca told you that the army was distributing weapons to the local Serbs. When did this conversation with Sveto Draca occur?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Sveto was with us every day. We grew up together, we went to school together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when it was that Sveto told you that the army was distributing weapons to local Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Immediately after the elections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please approximate what month that was.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: May, June, I don't know. I really can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the first paragraph of page 3 of Exhibit P490, you state that: "There were too many paramilitary units in the area during this time. They were with the regular army. They all wore camouflage uniforms and most were unshaven, had long hair, and they all had weapons. You could first see these paramilitaries with the regular army in June, July, 1991." My question to you, sir, is what colour camouflage was worn by these paramilitary groups?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Those camouflage uniforms were greenish yellowish black. As for the paramilitaries and those men who came, and when they went against Krusevo, they went together, the paramilitaries and the JNA. And the latter, the JNA, had olive-drab uniforms. Actually, they all had olive-drab uniforms usually worn by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the paramilitary units wear any insignias?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: The Krajina police or the Krajina milicija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of weapons did these paramilitary units possess?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned one incident with respect to Krusevo. Where else would you see the paramilitary units with the army?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Around Benkovac. They were in Benkovac. You couldn't go to Benkovac without being searched by them. Some 15 or 20 of them would point their rifles at you. So what could you do? Nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 2475 of Exhibit P491, you stated that you were not able to travel between Bruska and Benkovac in 1991 and stated that there were barricades when you went to Medvidja and Benkovac. Who were the people that were standing guard --

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, who were the people that were standing guard at these barricades?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: In the direction of Medvidja, those were the locals of Medvidja. And those who stood guard around Benkovac, hailed from around Benkovac, from the neighbouring villages there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any members of the paramilitary units that you described present at these barricades?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they present at all the barricades, or were they only present at certain individual barricades?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: It depended on the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where -- were the Krajina milicija that you've described or those individuals wearing those insignias present at barricades?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the Krajina milicija present at barricades?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The last time I went to Benkovac and back. And that was actually the last time I ever went to Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them present at any other barricades besides the barricades in the area of Benkovac?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Didn't go anywhere else. There was no chance for us to go anywhere else, to go through them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 2512 of Exhibit P491, you stated that: "When people moved out of Bruska, then this Captain Dragan came, and that's where they set up these training grounds, and they were training their army there." When did the people you are referring to move out of Bruska?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: I went on the 21st of December. That's when I left. And they must have left around the 28th of December. They were all moved out from there. I wasn't there so I'm not able to give you the exact date. By then I was already in hospital in Knin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These other people who moved out of Bruska, what was their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these individuals who later moved out of Bruska civilians or members of any armed forces?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 2513 of Exhibit P491, you were asked the question: "What was the connection between centre Alfa and Captain Dragan? How did you make this connection?" You answered: "That's what they called it. Well, no, they -- they set this up. It was called scientific centre Alfa" --

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: That was the Alfa centre, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, thank you. I will finish your quote. I will reread your full quote, and then I do have a question for you. Your answer was: "That's what they called it. Well, no, they -- they set this up. It was called scientific centre Alfa, I don't know, that's what it was called." Sir, if I could --

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's where the Special Police officers were trained. I saw that on video-clips, but I wasn't there. I don't know what they did there. The only way I can talk about that is to tell you what I saw on video-clips. We found some materials there, and we reviewed them. I wasn't there while this was going on to be able to tell you what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, that is quite clear from your previous testimony. I'm going to finish your statement from the Martic case. You continue to state: "Then this Captain Dragan was there, and that's where he trained soldiers, policemen, whatever he was training. I don't know, but judging by what we saw, this footage, you can see everything." Sir, my question to you is that, in your previous testimony, you referred to "they" called it centre Alfa, and "they set this up." Who were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: The Serbs. The Krajina police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These Special Police forces that were being trained there, are these the same Krajina milicija that you've previously mentioned here today or a different group of Special Police?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you are asking me too much. I told you what I'd seen. I don't know where they were from, who they were, where they had come from. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you describe seeing footage. What type of uniforms or insignias were the individuals wearing in this footage?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: The Special Police of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weber. Which Defence team will cross-examine the witness first? Mr. Bakrac, it will be you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it will be me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Bakrac. Mr. Bakrac is counsel for Mr. Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The presiding judge has introduced me to you. And before I start putting questions to you, I would firstly like to say a few words on behalf of Mr. Simatovic and on behalf of our Defence team and express our condolences for the tragedy that you experienced. The questions that I'll have for you will not go against what you experienced. I'm not going to try to of prove that the incident did not happen. I'll just try and shed light on some things that you have already stated. Can I begin?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic, you explained that you had resided in the village of Bruska and that the village had about 400 inhabitants; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that out of the 400 inhabitants, there are five Serb houses or households; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Since you spoke about 400 inhabitants, when you say five houses, are we talking about some 20 people altogether?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: It could have been four, three, or five more, but you can easily say that there were about 20 people living in those houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Marinovic, is it correct that in your village Bruska multiparty elections took place and that there was the local HDZ aboard?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it true that in your village Bruska, there was a local board of the Croatian Democratic Union, the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic, did you or any of your family members belong to the HDZ? Were you members of the HDZ or the local board of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No, none of us were, but I did vote for the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that you had seen posters, my learned friend asked you, but I would like the other side to be heard for the general public. You said that you heard the SDS posters, but were there also HDZ posters?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. There were both, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did those posters depicted Franko Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic, is it correct that already at the time it was known that the HDZ had promised that if they came into power, the Serbs would lose the status of a constituent people in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about politics. I do not engage in politics.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic, your answers so --

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: I still continue to give you fair answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I know that you don't engage in politics, but I believe that this was a notorious fact. Let me ask you again, did you hear that on television that there were some disputes about that and that the Serbs rebelled because of that, because of the announcements that if the HDZ won in the elections, they would be thrown out of the constitution as the constituent people?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Why couldn't they be a minority?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you are saying that you know that they were supposed to become a minority, and now you are wondering why shouldn't they be a minority, why shouldn't that be the case?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Marinovic. Mr. Marinovic, you said that you were a member of the reserve police from 1990.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you become a member of the reserve police immediately after the HDZ won in the elections in your village?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: As a reserve police officer, did you have a uniform? Did the others have uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: As the reserve police force and a reserve policeman, did you bear arms?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic, do you know that the HDZ armed its members? I'm not referring to you personally, but were you familiar with the fact?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was known, but we could not obtain weapons at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: As a member of the reserve police, you said that you were supposed to defend your village as reserve policemen.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Not to defend it, but to protect it. What were we supposed to defend it with?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What was your duty when it came to protecting your village?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: If something happened we were there to guard the village, and if something happened we would alert the others to flee.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you you report to anybody about what you saw in -- on the ground?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No, nobody, just to the others in the village. Who was I supposed to report to?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, my learned friend asked you earlier today whether you recognised paramilitaries at the barricades. Just a moment, please, bear with me. Could you please wait for me to finish my question and then start answering. Did I understand you properly that at the barricades you noticed members of the JNA, members of the police of Krajina, and the paramilitaries? Or when you say paramilitaries, did you only mean members of the Krajina police?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I meant. The Krajina police who were actually paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So what you are saying is that they were members of JNA and members of the Krajina police, and the latter were, for you, paramilitaries; right?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now, tell me please, when we are talking about the barricades, could you give us the time-frame?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of August 1991. Or before August, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were the barricades put up in front of the entrances into Serb villages or villages with a majority Serbian population?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: It was all one road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. I agreed with you that there was a barricade, but please tell me whether the barricades were also put up in front of the villages or settlements with predominantly Serbian population.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that there were attacks on Krusevo. Did you ever notice any attack on any other village in your environment?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: I could not notice any because all the villages were at a distance, and I saw the attack on Krusevo when they were pounding the village from Medvidja, and I saw lorries and tanks moving in from Benkovac against Krusevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether there is a special reason why of all Croatian villages, the JNA would attack only Krusevo and nothing else, no others?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: But it was not only Krusevo. There were other villages from Benkovac, Jesenice, Lepure, Luksic, Bunic, but I could not see all those village, they were at a distance from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And do you know that in Krusevo there was an armed HDZ unit deployed there or, rather, members of the Croatian police?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: They defended their own state.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not discussing that with you. That is your point of view, which I respect and which I value. My question was whether there were members of the HDZ and ZNG in Krusevo and in all those places where fighting took place.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: There was the Croatian police there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did they call themselves the Zengas ZNGs?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: I did not hear that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did they call themselves the national guards?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: I did not hear that I was not close to there. I couldn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic, please make a little pause after the question has been put to you and slow down your speed of speech, because if you want us to hear your testimony, you should speak at a speed which can be followed by our interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic, I would like to repeat that I don't intend to discuss things with you. I'm just trying to establish what the truth is, and so far my impression has been that you are fully prepared to tell the truth. That's why I would like to clarify some things. There's no need for you to provide hasty answers or argue with me. Mr. Marinovic, when you mentioned the police of Krajina at the barricades, did you mean local Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Ninety per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And when you say 90 per cent, you are not sure who the other 10 per cent were because you could not know all of them by name, could you?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: How was I supposed to know all of them? I didn't know all of them, of course. But I knew those who lived around me, I knew them, and I used to see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic, on the 21st of December when the unfortunate incidents struck your family, and this is an understatement because it was a tragedy, there was a Serb with you?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was he wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it true that when you provided your statement in Zadar that you stated that he had worn an olive-drab uniform on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not true. He did not wear a uniform. No. That must be a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please tell us what was that Serb gentleman's occupation?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: He was a postman.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: That Serb when the three other men entered, and you say that they sported the insignia of the police of Krajina on their sleeves, did he try to tell them that he was a Serb, that they should not shoot at him, or anything to that effect?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: There was no time. He did not have the time to say any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, did you recognise any of the three?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: One of them. One of them I knew because we used to play football in the past. I did [as interpreted] know his first and last name, but I did see him at one of these matches we had in Medvidja.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So this one person, to the best of your knowledge, was a person who was from Medvidja, a village close to Bruska?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No, he was not from Medvidja. I think he was from Bilisane.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And Lisane is another village close to Bruska; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Bilisane.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't hear you correctly. So Bilisane is another local place near Bruska; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it is some 10 kilometres away from Bruska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you learn subsequently that these two other individuals were local Serbs, perhaps from the same village as the one that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No, some people say that they were from that village, some say he wasn't, but I didn't recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, but subsequently you heard from some other people that these two were also from Bilisane?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, what somebody else said, and you know -- people who -- hearsay and gossip, I don't know. But I just saw this one person that I recognised. I did not know these other two people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, I understood you clearly, but let us repeat for the transcript. You subsequently heard that these two men, these two other men were also from Bilisane.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: I never said that, nor did I ever hear that. I never said or heard anything, because I cannot say anything about things I did not see, and I won't say anything that I myself did not see or hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, sir, when members of what you call the paramilitaries came to your village before this day, before the 21st of December, and harassed you by saying things like, This is Serbia, you must leave, would you agree that these were people from Medvidja, this was a Serbian village near Bruska?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, when this tragedy occurred, other than these three men, did you see any other soldiers in Bruska on the 21st of December?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Except for the members of your family that you listed here, did you hear of anyone else in Bruska being killed on that 21st of December?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No, no one other than us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you explained who was in the house sitting and playing cards with you. Were there any children in the house sleeping?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, my late brother's children were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did anyone harass them or interfere with them in any way?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No, they were upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when you managed to pull out, wounded as you were, I believe that you managed to get to the village of Kalanjevo Draga; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Kalanjevo Draga.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was that a Serb village?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Whom did you go to see in that Serbian village Kalanjevo Draga?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: To Mirko Kaleja's [phoen] house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is he a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is he a Serb?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did he call the emergency service? And if so, was there an ambulance sent, and from where?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he didn't. It was his wife who called the emergency service.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. It was his wife. Where did the ambulance come from?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but they came about 20 minutes later, or 30 minutes at the most. I don't know where they had come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Where did the ambulance take you?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: To Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was Benkovac a Serb place?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, no, it wasn't a Serb place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How many Serb -- or, rather, was the majority of the population in Benkovac Serbian?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was about 50/50.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was the Serbian party in power at the time in Benkovac?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because the army armed them and then they chased Croats from the -- they expelled Croats from the surrounding villages away.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were there Serbs in uniform in the ambulance who took you then to Benkovac to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, the Chamber is wondering the relevance of who exactly called the ambulance and whether Benkovac was a Serb city or Serb village or not, because the charges are not that every Serb is wrong-doing or that people in Benkovac or ambulance drivers are doing wrong things, so, therefore, it's -- the Chamber doesn't understand what the relevance of most of your last series of questions would have been. It is already clear --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'll be very frank. I am not going into any analysis now, nor is this my final brief, but I'm just trying to point out that this may have been a fluke, an incident that just happened unrelated to anything else. And then I assume that I will finish with my cross-examination with -- by the end of this session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is to be established through questions like, Did the husband or the wife call the ambulance? That's -- well, if I wanted to establish that it was just an incident, nothing else, then I would -- but I leave it to you at this very moment. But just for you to be aware --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you allow me, I think it is relevant because if men wearing a military uniform take you to a hospital, then I assume that this cannot be treated as part of a plan, but rather -- well, I won't go into this any further. If you allow me another 10 minutes, I will complete my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, were you sent from Benkovac to Knin to the hospital to undergo surgery?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was Knin, too, under Serb control at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that a member of the Serbian milicija came to the hospital. From your statements it does not come out clearly. Did he question you, or did he just say, This Ustasha is to be liquidated?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He said that, and Dr. Ignjatovic was there, and he said, Sir, you just leave this room because this is -- I am the boss here and not you. And if I were to see that doctor again, I would roast a lamb in His Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So he did not question you in any ways, he just said what he said. And Dr. Ignjatovic was a Serb then threw him out of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, once you recovered did you go to Knin which was under Serb control to the bus station, get on a bus, and go to Benkovac by bus?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I went to Vode Polace to see my late brother's wife, that's where her parents were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I apologise, it is my error. So it wasn't Benkovac, it was Vode Polje. But you just went to the bus station there, got on a bus, and went to Vode Polje; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did not get on a bus in Vode Polace.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How did you go there?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: By bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't understand you then. Did you say you didn't get on a bus, but you just went by bus?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's a different question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And then when you reached Dobro Polje were you driven by car by an inspector who was a member of the police of Serbian Krajina? Was he an inspector, what was his name, and where did he take you from and where to?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: He took me from Benkovac to my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To Bruska?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who took you from Benkovac to Bruska?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that his name was Milan, but I can't remember his family name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could just have a clarification in here. I didn't exactly hear the translation. I don't know if Mr. Bakrac referred to policija or milicija in his original question at 26/4. But if we could be clear in that distinction when discussing this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, could you provide the relevant clarification including what you said in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, was the person who took you in his car from Benkovac to your house a member of the Krajina milicija?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: He was an inspector. I believe his name was Milan Puza or something like that. I may have forgotten, but I think it could easily have been Milan Puza.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say inspector, where was he an inspector and what institution?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: In Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: He was an inspector in Benkovac, I don't want to lead you, but I just want to ask you, was he an inspector of the Krajina milicija?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: At the time when this milicija Krajina inspector took you in his car from Benkovac to Bruska to your home, was Milan Martic at the time the minister the interior of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, witness, and I will take advantage of the five minutes that we have left before the break to ask you something about the science centre Alfa. You said quite honestly that you actually saw this after you saw the video-tapes that you had found. Now, I would like to put it to you that up until 1993 there was no science centre there at all. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't, because they came then.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well, tell us then, when you say science centre and you saw these video-clip, what could you see in the video-clip? What was being done at that centre?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, training for the army, Special Police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And what did you see? What kind of training was that?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was training. What could training consist of but training?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you served in the Yugoslav People's Army; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was that the type of training similar to what you had gone through when you served in the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, what was the difference?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we didn't shoot. I was in artillery while I was in the army, whereas these people, they underwent training, they had rifles shooting. I could see all of that. They came by helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, you are now telling us something about your own training, but was it while you were --

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wait, Mr. Marinovic, until the question has been phrased, then take a little break, then answer the question. And Mr. Bakrac is also invited to make a little break after you've answered the question. Please proceed. Wait until the question has been finished, Mr. Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic, I am afraid we did not understand each other. I may have been unclear, and I apologise. Now, you were telling us about your training in the JNA in a special branch. Now, I am asking you about the JNA infantry. Did they also undergo training and rifle shooting and so on?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't in infantry so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Marinovic, if you don't know, you don't. That's quite all right. Could you now just tell us something about the video-clips. Did you see this video-clip in Bruska, the people in Bruska, or did you see it on TV? Was it broadcast by the Croatian television after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't broadcast by the Croatian television. We found this at the centre, and we watched the video-clip ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say we found this, Mr. Marinovic, were you a member of the Croatian army, and did you participate in Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Very well. But if I understood you correctly, the video-tapes were found when the Croatian army liberated Bruska following Operation Storm; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And they did not seize those tapes but, rather, they let the local people like you take those video-tapes and then watch them; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Marinovic. Thank you for your answers. I have no further questions, Your Honours. And thank you for the time that you've allotted me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. Is there any need for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: One question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. -- I was informed that you would have no questions for the witness, but I should have asked you in court, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I ask two questions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, you are fully entitled to cross-examine the witness. It was mainly on the basis of this understanding that I didn't address you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Jordash. Mr. Jordash is counsel for Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Can you hear me? Good afternoon. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, can you hear Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I've just got two --

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- or three questions. In Exhibit P491, your previous testimony, page 2513, with reference to the scientific centre Alfa, at line 12 and 13 you are commenting on who or what is being trained by Captain Dragan, and you state: "Then this Captain Dragan was there, and that's where he trained soldiers, policemen, whatever he was training, I don't know." Today when commenting on the training, you have focused and labelled the training as training of Krajina police.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honours, page 13 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So at the time of your previous testimony, you were stating that you did not know who or what was being trained, and now you say Krajina police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection, that is a misstatement of the testimony. I believe he did say that they were policemen. It was not further explored at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's any challenge to a quote, could you literally ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I did read the quote precisely from the transcript, page 2513, where the witness said: "That's where he trained soldiers, policemen, whatever he was training, I don't know."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: But then the following question, I believe, stated it differently than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But, Mr. Jordash is free to -- if you think that the other part is relevant and it should be put to the witness, you can do it in re-examination, Mr. Weber. And at the same time Mr. Jordash is aware that it doesn't bring him very much to be incomplete if there's a risk that the next lines are considered to be relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I inquire from the Prosecution, because I certainly don't want to be fair, but I cannot see the context that my learned friend wants me to put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but then we should first ask the witness to take off his earphones. Mr. Marinovic, could you take off your earphones for a second. Mr. Weber, is any chance that the witness would understand or speak English?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I do not believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, in the previous testimony there were follow-up questions that were being asked to the witness by the Trial Chamber. The witness did indicate that there were policemen, and it wasn't further explored. So to state that the witness didn't ask this, I believe is misleading. The witness did indicate that there were policemen. I think a fair question might be -- would be, You didn't -- you were not asked or you did not mention that these were Krajina police at that time. The way it was phrased to the witness has the inference that he intentionally did not provide that information or did not know it at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could my learned friend indicate which part of the transcript he is referring to, so I may just find it and not mislead, if I am misleading, which I don't, at the moment, accept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we talking -- are we -- let me just check.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe it is -- the question that counsel is referring to -- and I'm sorry if I misunderstood this. It was follow-up questions by Mr. Black that were precipitated by Chamber questions. Point just being, that the witness was asked a brief question about this, and he did say policemen. There was no exploring who the policemen was that he was referring to at the time. As consistent with the 92 ter practice, Prosecution asked further explanation of the evidence he provided. I believe counsel's reference to this here today is misleading because he is inferring that the witness didn't provide such information or didn't know that information at that time in 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, my learned friend cannot point to a part of the transcript which I ought to be putting to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's the same part that was referred to. I'm just asking that it be accurately -- the follow-up question. The part put to him was perfectly fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Black in the transcript says, Thanks very much. No further questions. And the -- I really do not see what my learned friend is referring to. I'm referring to the witness saying, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's get -- what page exactly are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm looking at 2513, Your Honour. I'm not sure what my learned friend is looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm looking at the exact same section; however, on page 30, lines 22 to 24, the follow-up question was: "So at the time of your previous testimony" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But let me just, am I right that you are referring to the evidence the witness gave today in this case; and you are referring to the evidence the witness gave in the Martic case?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I'm referring to two. I'm referring to the transcript where the witness clearly says, I don't know. And then to the evidence today where the witness is more specific. There may not be an inconsistency, but the witness ought without, in our submission, my learned friend jumping up, be given a chance to explain that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that -- one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, the objection is denied. Mr. Jordash can proceed as he did. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'll be very brief --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's first -- oh, yes, he has his earphones on again. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you want me to read that section of the transcript from your previous testimony again so that you understand what I'm asking you and so that I don't in any way mislead you. When you were asked about the scientific centre Alfa and who was there, you answered line 12, page 2513: "Then this Captain Dragan was there, and that's where he trained soldiers, policemen, whatever he was training, I don't know." And today you were being specific and said that it was the Krajina police who were being trained. Could you explain why it was in the transcript in your previous testimony you said, I don't know, and today where you are specific and focused on Krajina police?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: I am just saying things that I saw myself and nothing else. How would I know whom they were training? Whether it was the police or milicija or the army, whoever, how would I know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness, and I've got nothing further except to express my client's sympathy for your tragic experience. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jordash. We would under normal circumstances take a break now, but how much -- only a few questions. Then I suggest that we try to conclude the evidence of this witness. Mr. Weber

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Marinovic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Today on page 19, line 22, you stated that approximately 90 per cent of the Special Police of the Krajina were local Serbs. Could you please tell us where the other 10 per cent came from?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, probably from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you able to hear these other individuals who you believe were from Serbia speak?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a leading question. He should rephrase the question to read, how do you know that they had come from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe the question was not leading. I was trying to be efficient with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, the proper phrasing of the question would have been, Were you able to hear these other individuals who you believed were probably from Serbia? That would be the appropriate way of putting that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if you want to establish, of course, that what he believed probably to be the case, then of course, it would be useful to lay a foundation for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, were you able to hear these other individuals who you believed were from Serbia speak?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't close to them. I never got close enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is the reason that you believe that these approximately 10 per cent of the other individuals from the Special Police of the Krajina came from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Because there was some Arkan person there, and he brought these people over.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When did this occur?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at the very start he brought -- this Arkan person, he brought them from Serbia. He was murdered in the meantime, I think saw that on TV or in the media. Whether he is alive or not alive, I don't know, but him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please give us an approximate date when you believe that this Arkan person brought over people that became members of the Special Policija of the Krajina from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, well, again my learned colleague is putting words into the witness's mouth. The witness did not say that these Arkan's Men later on became members of the Special Police. He only spoke about the barricades, the whole story, this exchange is about barricades, and the 10 per cent on the barricades. So I would really appreciate it if the witness -- if the Prosecution refrained from asking this type of question in redirect. This is not even proper for examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I'll invite Mr. Weber to rephrase his question. At the same time, if you just object to the question, there's no need to elaborate on how inappropriate it is to put certain questions and whether it is in chief or not. Just object to the question on technical grounds, and then we'll decide on the matter. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the question was directly phrased from the three previous answers. I'll restate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please give us an approximate date when you believe that this Arkan person brought over people that you have stated became members of the Special Police of the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, objection. Could Mr. Weber please point to the line where he said that these people who had been brought by Arkan later on became members of the Special Police in Krajina. Could he please point to that part of the testimony, and if I made an error, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: He is testifying to page 36, line 2 through 6, that because this Arkan person brought these people over from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the end of the day, I'm just trying to ask a simple date, approximately when this occurred that Arkan brought these people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The people who turned out then because whether they then became members of the Special Police or whether they were already, for example, it's not literally taken from the testimony, so you rephrased it slightly. But if you would be happy to ask for a date, please, I'll not stop you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm just asking you of the approximate date in which you believe Arkan brought these people over.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to object. The witness hasn't said Arkan brought the people over. He said "this Arkan person." We don't quite know what that means, but it's certainly quite different possibly to Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe we are just playing with semantics here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, Mr. Jordash is right. If you -- Witness Marinovic, you told us about people you believed came from Serbia, whether you could speak to them, and then you were asked what the reason was that you believed that these approximately 10 per cent of the other individuals from the Special Police of the Krajina came from Serbia, and you said, Because there was some Arkan person there, and he brought these people over. Now, Mr. Weber would like to put a question to you in relation to those persons having been brought over. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately when were these people brought over?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: At the very beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately when are you referring to? If you could please give an approximate month and year.

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: In April 1991, I believe that's when it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac, any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I know it's time for the break. I just have two quick questions. Further cross-examination Mr. Bakrac:

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us, when did you hear about this Arkan person for the first time?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, for the first time I heard about him when he was captured on Dinara near Knin. And when there was an exchange where he was exchanged, he was captured by the Croatian police, he had weapons with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And you saw this shown on Croatian television?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and he was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And my last question is, do you allow that it is possible -- because you said that you did not hear these 10 per cent of the people on the barricades, you did not hear them speak. Do you allow the possibility that those 10 per cent of the members were local Serbs that you did not know, because I assume that you did not know every single person from your area?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I didn't know everyone. How would I know who came from where?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Bakrac. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I just ask a follow-up, please. Further cross-examination by Mr. Jordash:

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could I just ask you this, you spoke about some Arkan person and people being brought over. Was this a rumour that you heard?

utterances.speaker: ANTE MARINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, very much. Nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jordash. Mr. Marinovic, this concludes your evidence. I would like to thank you very much for coming to the video location and for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties, and - although very limited by the Bench - I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then this also concludes the videolink. We will take a break. After the break I'll first deliver a decision which is relevant for the next witness to be called. I might have one or two observations. It will altogether not take more than seven to eight minutes, and then we'll start with the next witness. We'll resume at 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A few matters in relation to the testimony we've just heard. Mr. Bakrac, you asked the witness whether the witness had said in the Zadar statement that Sveto or the postman, or whatever you want to call him, did wear a uniform. The witness said, No, that's not what I said. And then you just continued. Now, either there is a reason why you think that the statement is not correctly put on paper and then you should pursue the matter, or there's no reason whatsoever, but then you should refrain from asking such a question. Because I didn't find anything about wearing a uniform in the Zadar statement of the witness. It may be that you have mixed it up with another witness who said something about a uniform. But -- Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The accused are not receiving the interpretation. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you now receive my words interpretation? I just made an observation about the technical part of the cross-examination of the previous witness. Mr. Bakrac, I didn't find anything, so therefore either there is some real issue, then explore it, or leave it. That's clear? Then another matter that struck the Chamber -- yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I can't find that part in his previous testimony. He was presented as having stated that Sveto did have a uniform and then at that trial he was not sure whether he did or did not have a uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you referred to the Zadar statement. You asked him about his statement. You didn't ask anything about the transcript from what I remember. You asked, Did you say that in the Zadar statement? The witness said, No. Where it was unclear whether he denied that it was true or whether he denied that he had said it, that has not even been clarified, and then you moved on. So, therefore, real issues, please explore them. It will assist the Chamber, but let's try to find them. There is another matter, Mr. Bakrac, but that's -- perhaps I should -- or perhaps address --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I may not have been clear in my he question. That's why the answer wasn't clear. I did not dwell too much upon it because I did not think it was at all relevant after all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you should have refrained from it entirely. There's another matter. We spent yesterday quite some time on the agreed facts. Mr. Petrovic, you'll certainly remember that I -- well, I won't say I had to force you into that, but at least to encourage you very much to pay serious attention to that. Now, in relation to that, today we heard from Mr. Bakrac that the event as such in Bruska was not challenged. Agreed fact A(I), SAO Krajina, and the number 4, reads: "On the 21st of December, 1991, ten civilians, including nine Croats, were intentionally killed in the village of Bruska and the hamlet of Marinovic. The names of victims that were identified are contained in annex A, part E. Now, in that part we find the names of the victims. The Chamber has great difficulties in understanding why you could not agree on this where at the same time when the witness is called you do not challenge it in any of the relevant parts. I mean, the date has not been challenged; that there were ten civilians, apart from this one question, did he wear a uniform, but you considered it not to be very relevant; including nine Croats, that was already clear for the statement, but you sought it to be confirmed, don't ask me why; but that there was one Serb was already clear from the statement; including nine Croats, were intentionally killed, that has not been challenged; in the village of Bruska in the hamlet of Marinovic, which has not been challenged; the names of the victims were not in any way challenged. So the only thing that then remains is their years of birth, but even there you did not ask one question about it. So I really -- it is said that you need an enormous amount of time; whereas, apparently preparing for these witnesses you look at it, and you do not challenge it. So why then not agree on it? Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you know that my colleague Mr. Petrovic and I are in a very dire position when it comes to the list of adjudicated facts. We would like to look at the whole list and be able to respond to the whole list. We can respond to individual incidents like the one in Bruska, for example, but that would be from time to time, every now and then. We've been given a dead-line, and we will make sure to investigate everything in order to be sure that things did happen. The incident in Bruska is just one of the incidents, or, rather, one of the events involving casualties, and that's one of those that we do not dispute. But we did not want to respond just to one or two events and leave the others until later. We wanted to look at the whole list and then respond to the whole list. You gave us a dead-line yesterday. We will try and respect it, but please bear in mind that we got involved in the case when we did. There are many other things that we are trying to do at the same time, and, therefore, we are begging your indulgence and understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's on record. I just wanted to let you know that you also, of course, could have informed the Prosecution prior to presenting this witness that there was no dispute about this and this and this and this, and even if that would not have been a final response to the proposal for adjudicated facts. I would like to read a decision relevant for the witness to come. And I already informed the booth that there are slight changes compared to the written version, specifically in the reference to another case. This is the Chamber's decision on the Prosecution's motion for the augmentation of protective measures for witness JF-035. In its motion filed the 7th of May, 2010, the Prosecution requested the Chamber to augment the protective measures currently in place for witness JF-035 and to allow his testimony to be given entirely in closed session. Witness JF-035 was previously granted protective measures in another case before this Tribunal. On the 13th of May, 2010, the Prosecution indicated to the Chamber through an informal communication that witness JF-035 is very anxious about his scheduled testimony and that knowing the Chamber's decision would set his mind at ease. On the same day, the Chamber asked the Stanisic Defence and the Simatovic Defence in court to file any responses to the Prosecution's motions by the close of business on the 17th of May, thus shortening the time-period for responses pursuant to Rule 126 bis of the rules. And this can be found at transcript pages 4949 and 4950. On the 14th of May, 2010, both Defence teams informed the Chamber through an informal communication that they did not wish to file any responses to the motion. On the 18th of May, 2010, the Chamber informed the parties, again through an informal communication, that it had decided to grant the Prosecution's motion and that this decision would be put on the record at a later stage. In its motion, the Prosecution submits that witness JF-035 has particularly serious security concerns and that, in spite of the protective measures granted in the other case, witness JF-035 and his family were subject to numerous death threats directly connected with his testimony in that case. The Prosecution submits, therefore, that it is apparent that the protective measures granted to witness JF-035 in the other case before the Tribunal were insufficient to protect his identity. Pursuant to Rule 75(I) of the rules. The Chamber has consulted with those judges who initially granted the protective measures to witness JF-035 and who remain judges of the Tribunal. Further, pursuant to Rule 75(J) of the rules, the Chamber has made inquiries with the Victims and Witness Section and can confirm that witness JF-035 fully consents to the augmented protective measure of closed session. The requirements of Rule 75(I) and (J) of the rules are therefore fulfilled. Having considered the threats received by witness JF-035 following his testimony in the other case before this Tribunal, the Chamber finds that the protective measures granted at that time were insufficient and that the only effective way to protect his identity is to hear his testimony in closed session. For the foregoing reasons, pursuant to Rule 75 of the Rules, the Chamber grants the Prosecution's motion and orders that witness JF-035 give his testimony in closed session. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. We turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, you would -- yes. Thank you, we are back in open session. I understand there was something you would like to put on the record, please do to.
